I designed the seven onboarding screens on the [Onboarding](https://ponzu.design/canvases/cnv_evala1?page=pg_or0j0) page, using the colours and font from your spec. One change from the obvious choice: the text on the orange buttons is dark, because white on that orange is too low-contrast to read well.

cases.prDescription: ## Onboarding flow design Designs the seven onboarding screens from `docs/onboarding/README.md` as iPhone screens (390×844) on the [Cadence onboarding canvas](https://ponzu.design/canvases/cnv_evala1): Welcome, Goal, Experience, Schedule, Reminders, Building plan and Your plan, left to right on the Onboarding page. ### What changed in the repo `docs/onboarding/README.md` gets a **Design** section that links the canvas and records the decisions and open questions. ### Decisions - Uses the spec's tokens: paper #F6F2EA, ink #16130F, signal orange #FF5A1F, muted #6F6A62, Inter Tight. - Main button text is ink, not white. White on #FF5A1F is about 3.1:1, and ink on it is about 5.9:1. - Orange appears only where the spec puts it: the main button, the selected days and the plan label. Selected options get an ink outline with a small orange check. - Goal, Experience, Schedule and Reminders share a back button and a four-part progress bar. - The Reminders screen states the product rule (one notification, training days only), and its bells follow the days picked on Schedule. - Your plan shows the full week, rest days included. ### Open questions - **Trial and paywall:** these aren't decided in the product notes, so the flow has no paywall screen. - **Account creation:** the spec doesn't cover it. Welcome offers sign-in for returning users. - Session names and the 7:00 AM reminder default are placeholders. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

cases.closing:
It comes after [4 Schedule](https://ponzu.design/canvases/cnv_evala3?artboard=ab_r2vm9jf) because the reminder is about the training days. Once you've picked Mon/Wed/Fri/Sun, [5 Reminders](https://ponzu.design/canvases/cnv_evala3?artboard=ab_7vzvpg2) can promise something specific, "Upper body, 30 min on Wednesday at 7:30, never on rest days", instead of a cold "Allow notifications?" at launch. That matters because iOS only lets the app show the system prompt once, so asking when the value is clearest gives the best chance of a yes.

That's my reading of the design, though. Neither the spec nor the flow note says why it was ordered this way. One possible catch: if accounts come after the plan, someone who drops out at the account step has already been asked for notifications. If you want the reasoning written down, I can add it to the flow note. Nothing is changed or committed, and there's no pull request.
